name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. This gives us a clean baseline to measure its review quality before expanding to open PRs. The trade-off is delaying broader deployment until we validate the tool’s accuracy on already-closed work.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs trains reviewers to ignore real issues because the model’s feedback arrives after the work is already approved and merged. Better: run PR-Agent live on open PRs but cap its scope to non-blocking comments—this tests its utility without delaying reviews or creating false confidence in post-hoc validation. Settle it by measuring the delta in review time and merge quality between capped live runs and shadow mode on the same PRs over two weeks.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* open and merged PRs from day one—this catches real-time issues while still building a baseline for accuracy. The extra compute cost is negligible compared to the risk of missing critical feedback in open PRs.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent live on open PRs but restrict its comments to non-blocking suggestions only. This tests its real-world utility without slowing down reviews or creating merge conflicts. The trade-off is accepting some noise in PRs—irrelevant or low-value comments—until we tune its precision.
